activeEvents.intro: A live register of high-impact weather events worldwide — tropical cyclones, floods, droughts and wildfires — each placed on the map and ranked by alert level. Use the region filter to isolate any part of the world. This is the repository's front door: what is active now, where, and how severe.
activeEvents.note: Seeded snapshot of major active events, web-verified to 5–19 Aug 2026. Alert levels here are indicative, assigned from cited severity; running fetch_events.py replaces this list with the live GDACS feed and its official green / orange / red levels. Sources: GDACS, EFFIS (Europe), NIFC (US), national disaster authorities.

activeEvents.inference: Mid-August 2026 is defined by fire and water. Wildfire is the dominant hazard on two continents at once — the US Northwest at Preparedness Level 5, and a record Mediterranean season (Spain and France both at national records, EFFIS well above its 20-year average). The wet signal runs through South and East Asia, where the Indian and Pakistani monsoons are the deadliest active events. Europe carries both fire and a slow-onset drought; the tropics are quiet, with Hurricane Lala the only significant system. The registry lengthens once the live GDACS feed is wired in — this snapshot captures the current headline events.
